newsitem.title: SPAIN: FOCUS-Spain moves towards telephone competition.
newsitem.headline: FOCUS-Spain moves towards telephone competition.

text.p: Spain took the first step on Friday towards launching the country's second telecommunications operator, Retevision, just a few weeks after concluding privatisation of the giant competitor Telefonica.

The government said it would privatise a 60 percent stake in the state telecommunications group Retevision, which is expected start a basic domestic phone service in competition with Telefonica by the end of this year.
Retevision's privatisation will open up to foreign competitors a 1.4 billion peseta ($9.7 million) per year business.
France Telecom and Deutsche Telekom have already joined up with Spain's Banco Central Hispano to bid in the restricted auction, where the minimum purchase price was set at 45 billion pesetas.
But more groups are seen joining the fray.
Two of Spain's utility firms, Empresa Nacional de Electricidad (Endesa) and Union Fenosa have shown interest in taking a stake in the new Retevision.
But Spaniards are expected to gain the most if telephone tariffs are pushed lower by heightened competition.
Retevision's chairman, Pedro de Torres, said in December that the main goal of the company would be to compete aggressively with Telefonica. "Tariffs are abnormally high," said Torres.
The government seems eager to give Retevision a hand.

It is expected to approve a cheap connecting cost with the Telefonica, setting a price at between two and 2.5 pesetas per minute versus the seven pesetas the domestic telephone operator had requested, local financial press reported.
The measure could allow Retevision to offer calls, especially long-distance, at cheap rates, triggering a tariff war which should benefit Spaniards.
"If these price expectations are met, that would be in favour of Retevision," one industry source told Reuter.
But at the moment, Telefonica has proved itself nimble and able to face competition where it has to.
Industry experts said that, for example, it reacted very well to the competition of 'call back' operators, which are offering cheaper international phone prices in Spain.
In the last 12 months, Telefonica has cut its international tariffs around 20 percent with the last reduction of around 8.8 percent effective on Saturday.
As a result, turnover in pesetas in international phone services fell 4.4 percent to 140 billion pesetas at the telecommunications giant.
Telefonica proved to be aggressive in the dynamic mobile phone sector also, ending 1996 with 2.3 million contracts versus the 650,000 clients of its competitor Airtel.
Airtel, in which British Telecommunications Plc (BT) has an 8.5 percent stake, could be a natural partner of Retevision as both are expected to fight against Telefonica.

Telefonica's domestic basic tariffs have been frozen since 1994. If the two domestic operators are not enough for a brisk competitive market, the government has already announced its intention to start a third operator.
-- Madrid Newsroom, + 341 585 8340 ($ = 144.7 Spanish Pesetas)
